edges.effect_quant: CA125-based surveillance in women with hereditary or strong familial risk can improve the positive predictive value of an abnormal screen and can be tuned by menopausal status or longitudinal algorithms, but available cohorts still show interval cancers and frequent advanced-stage disease, so detection performance remains inconsistent rather than clearly reassuring.
edges.population: women at high inherited or family-history-based risk for tubo-ovarian cancer undergoing CA125-centered surveillance
edges.mechanism: Serial CA125 measurement can flag rising tumor-marker trajectories before overt symptoms, especially when personalized thresholds or longitudinal change algorithms are used, but biologically aggressive serous cancers may still emerge between screens.
edges.summary: This is a mixed detection edge. CA125 surveillance is more informative in higher-risk women than in the general population, yet it still misses some clinically important cancers and has not solved the interval-cancer problem that motivates risk-reducing surgery in BRCA carriers.
edges.caveats: Most high-risk screening evidence is observational and often combines CA125 with ultrasound or other markers, so the independent contribution of CA125 is not always isolatable. This edge concerns detection performance, not mortality reduction, and should not be read as an alternative to guideline-supported risk-reducing salpingo-oophorectomy for eligible mutation carriers.
